dossier.valuation_method: Probability-weighted composite of three multi-stage DCFs (decline-vs-stabilization) at 13.5% cost of capital, cross-checked with peer EV/EBITDA and normalized-FCF yield.
dossier.thesis_summary: Nu Skin is a high-quality operator of a structurally declining direct-selling (MLM) franchise: revenue down 45% from its 2021 peak and the field force (Customers -45%, Paid Affiliates -52%, Sales Leaders ~-50%) collapsed with it, yet it remains FCF-positive (~$80M normalized), near net-cash on funded debt, pays a covered dividend, and earns a 77.7% core gross margin. Value hinges on whether the decline stabilizes and whether Prysm iO plus LatAm/India restore growth. Bear ($7.62), base ($10.36) and bull ($14.06) DCFs at 13.5% give a probability-weighted FMV of ~$10.30.
key_value_drivers: Trajectory of the secular revenue decline (Sales Leaders the key leading indicator)
Prysm iO subscription flywheel / subscriber LTV
LatAm (+53% YoY) and India (late-2026) offset to China/Korea/N.A. erosion
Near-net-cash balance sheet and ~$80M normalized FCF
key_risks: Decline never inflects (Q1 2026 -12%; Sales Leaders -13% to -19%)
Prysm iO switching-cost transition accelerates attrition; health-claim FTC/biometric risk
Inventory obsolescence on 147 days of pre-bought stock
Emerging-market mix dilutes premium margins; FY2026 EPS step-down to ~$1.00
what_would_change_my_mind: Two+ quarters of decelerating decline with Customers/Sales Leaders flattening
Prysm iO subscriber growth well above +5%/+14% with disclosed conversion/LTV data
Core GM >=77% with selling ~40% through the mix shift
Conversely: decline re-accelerating, a China event, an inventory write-down, or a dividend/buyback cut
